recipe: If building a new web palette, author it in OKLCH. Lightness and chroma shift predictably there, so ramps stay perceptually even without hand-correcting every step.
trigger_condition: Are you defining a new colour palette for web?

recipe: Build roles, not a bag of swatches: surfaces, text, actions, borders, semantic states. A colour without an assigned job becomes decoration and drifts across screens.
trigger_condition: Are you adding colours that have no assigned role?

recipe: Tint neutrals toward the brand hue only when it buys genuine cohesion. Untinted grey is a legitimate choice; reflexive tinting is cargo-cult, not craft.
trigger_condition: Are you tinting greys without a stated reason?

recipe: Never grey text on a coloured surface. Derive secondary text from that surface hue or its foreground; generic washed grey reads as an unstyled bug.
trigger_condition: Is secondary text sitting on a non-neutral coloured surface?

recipe: Minimum contrast: 4.5:1 body text, 3:1 large text, 3:1 controls, icons and focus indicators. Placeholder text counts as body text, not decoration.
_note: near-duplicate of :143 (text contrast, WCAG-sourced) and :144 (non-text contrast)
_review_reason: near-duplicate of :143 (text contrast, WCAG-sourced) and :144 (non-text contrast)

recipe: Do not eyeball contrast. Compute it, and check every interactive state, overlay, text-on-image, disabled content, and both themes rather than only the resting default.
Do not hold high chroma at extreme lightness just to make a ramp numerically uniform. Near-white and near-black steps should shed saturation to stay believable.
trigger_condition: Are you generating a tonal ramp algorithmically?

recipe: Dark mode is a design pass, not an inversion. Re-derive surface elevation and contrast explicitly; a mechanically flipped light theme reads muddy and flat.
trigger_condition: Are you adding dark mode to an existing light theme?

recipe: In dark themes avoid pure #000 as the page ground. It crushes elevation cues and leaves shadows nowhere to go; use a near-black surface instead.
trigger_condition: Is a dark theme's page ground pure #000?
_original_recipe: Avoid pure black and pure white as ground. Pure black crushes elevation cues, leaves shadows nowhere to go, and reads as unfinished rather than dramatic.
_review_reason: pure-white half is unsupported by the cited source and overstated; the reasoning only covers black grounds in dark themes

recipe: Keep semantic colour meanings stable across themes and screens, but defer to platform and domain convention. Red means falling in some markets and rising in others.
trigger_condition: Does this product ship across regions or platforms?

recipe: If colour carries information, add a second channel: text, icon, shape, or position. Colour-only encoding fails for colour-blind users and vanishes in greyscale.
trigger_condition: Does any status or category rely on colour alone?

recipe: Let the strongest colour own one deliberate region rather than scattering tiny accents. Confetti accent use reads as indecision, not energy.
trigger_condition: Is the accent appearing in several unrelated small places?

recipe: Spend the primary action colour on the primary action. If decoration also wears it, the button stops being findable and the hierarchy quietly collapses.
trigger_condition: Does decoration share the primary action colour?

recipe: If a surface uses five or more hues, cut to one or two plus neutrals. Colour count is almost never what made the design feel rich.
trigger_condition: Does the palette exceed two hues plus neutrals?

recipe: Colour applied without hierarchy, state, or content relationship is paint, not a strategy. For each hue, name what it distinguishes from what.
Pick a posture before picking hues: restrained (neutrals plus one accent), committed (one colour at 30-60 percent), full palette (3-4 roles), or drenched (colour as subject).
trigger_condition: Have you decided how much colour the surface carries?

recipe: If a surface feels loud, drop saturation to roughly 70-85 percent of full before removing elements. Saturation is usually the noise, not the element count.
trigger_condition: Does the interface feel busy rather than crowded?

recipe: Purple-to-blue gradients, neon cyan, and glassmorphism are the default AI palette. If you reached for them without a brief reason, you defaulted rather than chose.
trigger_condition: Did the brief actually ask for this treatment?

recipe: Avoid gradient-filled text. It degrades legibility, makes contrast unmeasurable, and is usually decoration substituting for a hierarchy decision you have not made.
trigger_condition: Are you filling type with a gradient?

recipe: Use 1rem/16px as the ordinary web body-text floor. Go smaller only for a genuinely dense or secondary role, or where platform convention or user settings justify it.
_original_recipe: 16px is the web body floor. Drop to 14px only for genuinely secondary text, and never below 16px on mobile inputs, which force-zoom in iOS Safari.
_review_reason: source qualifies the floor; the iOS input-zoom clause duplicates :157

recipe: Hold prose between 45 and 75 characters per line, 65-75 for sustained body copy. Past that the eye loses the return and skips lines.
trigger_condition: Is this a block of running prose?

recipe: Tune line height inversely with measure: wider columns need more leading. A single fixed line-height across every column width is a guess, not a system.
trigger_condition: Does text appear at more than one column width?

recipe: Light text on dark surfaces needs compensation on all three axes: slightly more line height, a touch more tracking, and one step more weight when the face needs it.
trigger_condition: Is body text set light-on-dark?
_original_recipe: Light text on dark surfaces needs compensation on three axes at once: slightly more line height, a touch more tracking, and one step more weight.
_review_reason: source says one step more weight only when the face needs it; recipe made it unconditional

recipe: Heading, body, label, metadata, and data must be distinguishable at a glance. Two roles one small step apart in size and weight read as one role.
Make scale and weight steps obvious. A two-pixel size difference between tiers is noise the reader cannot resolve, so it buys no hierarchy at all.
trigger_condition: Are adjacent type tiers close in size or weight?

recipe: Use the fewest families and roles that make the hierarchy unmistakable. A second family needs a stated job, not a mood.
trigger_condition: Are you introducing a second typeface?

recipe: When simplifying: one family, three to four sizes, two to three weights. Most interfaces that feel busy are over-typeset rather than over-populated.
trigger_condition: Is the interface being simplified or decluttered?

recipe: Cap display type near 6rem and set a tracking floor of -0.04em. Tighter than that and letterforms collide at the sizes where collisions are most visible.
trigger_condition: Are you setting oversized display or hero type?

recipe: Choose paragraph spacing or first-line indent, not both. Combining them double-marks the boundary and reads as a formatting error rather than a choice.
trigger_condition: Are you setting multi-paragraph running text?

recipe: Ship only the weights and character ranges actually used, preload critical faces, and set font-display swap or optional so text never renders invisible during load.
trigger_condition: Are you loading a webfont?

recipe: Provide metric-compatible fallbacks. A fallback with different metrics turns the font swap into a layout jump the user reads as the page breaking.
trigger_condition: Are you loading a webfont?

recipe: Never defeat browser zoom, user font settings, Dynamic Type, or platform text scaling. Test at 200 percent zoom and confirm containers grow with the text.
_note: near-duplicate of :152 (200% zoom and platform text scaling), which is more specific
_review_reason: near-duplicate of :152 (200% zoom and platform text scaling), which is more specific

recipe: Do not make type decorative at the expense of comprehension. If the reader has to decode the letterforms, the typeface has become the content.
_note: generic filler with no actionable criterion
_review_reason: generic filler with no actionable criterion

recipe: Inter, Arial, and the raw system stack are what everything already uses. If the brief asked for a voice, a default face is the absence of one.
trigger_condition: Does the brief call for a distinct brand voice?

recipe: Monospace signals code, data, or machine output. Worn as a stylistic costume over ordinary prose it reads as borrowed credibility rather than precision.
trigger_condition: Is the content actually code, data, or machine output?

recipe: If numbers update in place or align in columns, set `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`. Proportional digits make aligned figures jitter on every refresh.
trigger_condition: Do numbers update in place or align in columns?
_original_recipe: If numbers update in place or align in columns, set tabular numerals. Proportional digits make aligned figures jitter on every refresh.
_review_reason: add the actual CSS so the hint is actionable

recipe: Avoid a small kicker/eyebrow label above a heading. It is a template tell that adds a hierarchy tier carrying no information.
trigger_condition: Are you adding a small label above a heading?
_original_recipe: Impeccable bans the small kicker label above a heading outright. It is a template tell that adds a hierarchy tier carrying no information.
_review_reason: drop the source-name framing; state the guidance directly

recipe: Use clamp for fluid type rather than a ladder of breakpoint overrides, then verify the computed minimum still clears the readable floor at the narrowest width.
trigger_condition: Does type size change across breakpoints?

recipe: Test headings with the real final copy at every breakpoint. Placeholder text hides the two-word orphan and the six-line mobile headline.
Use a 4-unit base spacing scale rather than 8-only. An 8-only scale misses the useful middle steps and forces off-scale one-off values.
trigger_condition: Are you defining a spacing scale from scratch?

recipe: Vary tight and generous intervals deliberately. Uniform spacing everywhere reads as a wireframe; contrast in spacing is what actually expresses grouping.
Group by meaning using proximity before reaching for containers, borders, or backgrounds. A card is what you add once spacing has already failed.
trigger_condition: Are you adding a container to show grouping?

recipe: Put more space above a heading than below it. The heading belongs to the content that follows, and symmetric spacing orphans it between blocks.
Prefer gap over child margins when the spacing expresses a sibling relationship. Margins leak across component boundaries and collapse unpredictably; gap does neither.
trigger_condition: Is the spacing between siblings in one container?

recipe: Match information density to use frequency, decision complexity, and visitor mode. A daily operator tool and a landing page cannot share a density setting.
Expose density as one coarse multiplier, roughly 0.6 to 1.4 with 1.0 default, and scale spacing against it rather than forking layouts per density.
trigger_condition: Does the product need more than one density mode?

recipe: Fix optical alignment as well as mathematical. Icons, punctuation, and round shapes need nudging off the grid in order to look on it.
Make responsive behaviour structural: reorder, collapse, reflow, or reveal based on what still matters at that width. Scaling pixels is resizing, not adapting.
At every breakpoint confirm DOM and focus order still match visual order. CSS reordering silently breaks keyboard sequence and screen-reader narration.
trigger_condition: Does any breakpoint reorder elements visually?

recipe: Break where the design breaks, not at device widths. Mobile 320-767, tablet 768-1023, desktop 1024 plus is a starting grid, never a specification.
trigger_condition: Are you choosing breakpoint values?

recipe: Flex and grid children need min-width 0, or min-height 0 on the block axis, to shrink below content size. Without it long strings blow out the layout.
trigger_condition: Can a flex or grid child hold unbounded text?

recipe: Reduce component nesting depth and eliminate stacked cards. A card inside a card inside a panel is three borders saying the same single thing.
trigger_condition: Is a card nested inside another card or panel?

recipe: A grid of identically sized cards is the default composition. If every item carries equal visual weight, you have not expressed a hierarchy, only a list.
trigger_condition: Do all grid items have identical size and weight?

recipe: On compact widths go single column with full-width components and move navigation to bottom or a disclosure. Never hide core functionality just to fit.
trigger_condition: Is the viewport below tablet width?

recipe: Respect safe areas and window insets in every configuration: notch, Dynamic Island, hinge, status bar, keyboard. On web use viewport-fit cover with env safe-area-inset.
trigger_condition: Does content reach the screen edge on a phone?

recipe: Multitasking is a size, not an edge case. iPad Split View and Android multi-window hand a tablet a phone-width window, so drive layout from size classes.
trigger_condition: Does the app run on tablets or foldables?

recipe: Budget 30-40 percent extra space for translated strings, and use logical properties like margin-inline-start so right-to-left works without a second stylesheet.
trigger_condition: Will this ship in more than one language?

recipe: If a layout feels cramped, add breathing room before removing content. Density rather than element count is usually what makes an interface feel cheap.
trigger_condition: Does the layout feel crowded?

recipe: Squint at the composition. If primary element, secondary element, and major groups do not emerge in that order, the hierarchy exists only in your intent.
Make one decisive move completely, then quiet everything around it so the move is legible. Boldness comes from contrast with neighbours, not from raising everything.
trigger_condition: Are you trying to make a design feel bolder?

recipe: To emphasise a section, reuse the existing motif and type scale at full strength rather than inventing new colours, radii, or shadows just for it.
trigger_condition: Are you emphasising one part of an existing design?

recipe: One primary action per view, a few secondary, everything else hidden. Two equally weighted primary buttons means the design has not decided what the screen is for.
trigger_condition: Does the view have more than one primary action?

recipe: Keep a single decision point at four options or fewer. Past that, group, stage, or default; the user is now comparing rather than choosing.
trigger_condition: Does one decision offer more than four options?

recipe: Four or fewer items held at once is manageable, five to seven strains, eight or more overloads. Chunk or stage anything past four.
trigger_condition: Must the user hold items in mind across steps?

recipe: Identify the 20 percent of the interface delivering 80 percent of the value and make it the essential layer. Everything outside is expendable or hideable.
trigger_condition: Are you deciding what to cut or hide?
_note: generic 80/20 platitude, no actionable criterion for what counts as essential
_review_reason: generic 80/20 platitude, no actionable criterion for what counts as essential

recipe: Cut redundant information, borders and shadows without function, hedging marketing copy, steps that collapse into earlier ones, and duplicate entry points to the same function.
trigger_condition: Are you simplifying an existing interface?

recipe: Removal has a floor. Never sacrifice necessary functionality, accessibility markup and labelling, decision-critical information, or task-completion clarity in the name of simplicity.
trigger_condition: Are you removing elements to simplify?

recipe: Build hierarchy from weight, size, and space before colour and boldness. Colour-led hierarchy stops working the moment a second colour enters the screen.
The first viewport is a thesis, not a header. Demonstrate the mechanism immediately rather than introducing it decoratively and deferring the proof below the fold.
trigger_condition: Is this a landing or marketing surface?

recipe: Across a long scroll vary density, scale, imagery, motion, and quiet inside one grammar. A dense passage earns a quiet one.
trigger_condition: Is this a long scrolling page?

recipe: Ask whether the composition could be lifted into a competitor product unchanged. If yes it is category-interchangeable, not designed for this product.
Gradients, glass, and generic icon tiles placed where real content belongs are the gap wearing chrome. Fill the gap rather than decorating it.
trigger_condition: Is decoration occupying a slot that wants content?

recipe: Smaller steps between sizes read calmer, larger steps read louder. Choose the step ratio from the emotional register you want, not from a default scale.
The row of three big numbers under a hero is a template, not a finding. Use it only when those metrics are the actual argument.
trigger_condition: Are you adding a stat row under a hero?

recipe: Reveal one thing at a time. A screen that teaches, explains, and requests input simultaneously gets none of the three done.
trigger_condition: Is the screen doing more than one job at once?

recipe: Numbered section labels imply an order the reader must follow. Use them for genuinely sequential content only, not to manufacture a sense of structure.
trigger_condition: Is the content actually sequential?

recipe: Every interactive control needs default, hover, focus-visible, active and disabled states; controls that trigger async work also need loading, error and success states.
_original_recipe: Every control needs default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, and success behaviour. Shipping three of eight is where looks-done-feels-broken comes from.
_review_reason: overstated: not every control has loading/success states

recipe: Design empty, loading, error, success, long-content, and missing-content states with real data. The happy path is the easy sixth of the work.
Distinguish first use, no results, filtered-to-nothing, no permission, and failure. One generic nothing-here message collapses five different user situations into one dead end.
trigger_condition: Can this list be empty for more than one reason?

recipe: An empty state names what belongs there, why it matters, and the one action that starts it. Illustration without a next step is wallpaper.
trigger_condition: Are you designing an empty state?

recipe: Use persistent labels. Placeholders are examples, not labels, and they vanish exactly when the user needs to check what the field wanted.
trigger_condition: Are you labelling a form field with a placeholder?

recipe: Buttons name their action with a specific verb and object. Yes, OK, and Submit force the user back to the dialog text to work out what happens.
For destructive actions name the object and the consequence in the control itself, and keep the same noun and verb the rest of the product uses.
trigger_condition: Is this action destructive or irreversible?

recipe: An error says what failed, why when known and useful, and how to recover. Missing the third part makes it an announcement rather than a message.
trigger_condition: Are you writing an error message?

recipe: Never lead with an internal error code, and do not overstate certainty about the cause. Codes belong as secondary detail for support, not as the message.
trigger_condition: Are you surfacing a system or API error?

recipe: Validation explains what needs attention and how to correct it without blaming the user. Put format and eligibility requirements before submission, not after rejection.
trigger_condition: Does this form validate input?

recipe: Preserve user input on error. Clearing a form after a failed submit is the most reliable single way to lose the user entirely.
trigger_condition: Can this form fail submission?

recipe: Loading text names the real operation and sets an honest expectation when the wait is meaningful. A bare spinner with Loading tells the user nothing.
trigger_condition: Is the wait long enough to notice?

recipe: Disable the control while its action is in flight. Without it the impatient second click becomes a duplicate charge, message, or record.
trigger_condition: Does this control trigger a non-idempotent action?

recipe: Map failures to what happened: validation detail for 400, permission explanation for 403, not-found for 404, support path for 500. Generic failure text serves none of them.
trigger_condition: Does this surface network or server errors?

recipe: Do not use a modal for a non-critical task. A modal claims the user whole attention and forfeits their context in order to get it.
trigger_condition: Is this task genuinely blocking or critical?

recipe: Do not reskin platform controls such as switches, pickers, steppers, alerts, and context menus for branding. Users hold muscle memory your version breaks.
trigger_condition: Are you restyling a native system control?

recipe: Do not port iOS controls into Android or the reverse. Action sheets and bottom sheets solve the same problem in two different grammars.
trigger_condition: Does this app ship on both iOS and Android?

recipe: Before adding a component variant, ask whether three versions already cover ninety percent of real use. A dozen variants is a system that stopped deciding.
trigger_condition: Are you adding another variant to a component?

recipe: If one component appears at several widths, make it respond to its own container (`container-type: inline-size` plus `@container` queries) instead of passing size props down or keying off viewport breakpoints.
trigger_condition: Does this component appear at multiple widths?
_original_recipe: If the same component appears in several contexts, make it container-aware rather than passing size props down. The component should read its own space.
_review_reason: vague; name the mechanism (container queries)

recipe: Never put functionality behind hover alone. Branch on input capability with `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` or `(pointer: coarse)`, not on viewport width.
trigger_condition: Is anything revealed only on hover?
_original_recipe: Never put functionality behind hover alone. Branch on capability with pointer coarse and hover hover media queries, not on viewport width.
_review_reason: media-query names were garbled ('pointer coarse and hover hover'); give real syntax

recipe: Past a few hundred rows, paginate or virtualise. Rendering ten thousand items at once is a design decision that shows up to the user as jank.
trigger_condition: Can this list grow past a few hundred items?

recipe: Onboarding gets the user to first value, it does not teach the product. Teach one thing at a time, cap it at three concepts, always allow skip.
trigger_condition: Are you designing a first-run or onboarding flow?

recipe: Track completion and respect dismissals. Showing the same tour or tooltip twice converts a helpful gesture into the thing users learn to close on sight.
trigger_condition: Does this hint or tour reappear across sessions?

recipe: 100-150ms for immediate feedback, 150-300ms for routine state change, 300-500ms for layout, overlay or view transitions, 500-800ms for one deliberately authored focal entrance.
Exit faster than entrance. A dismissal that takes as long as the arrival feels like the interface is arguing with the user about leaving.
For confident arrivals use exponential ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1). It moves fast then settles, which the eye reads as responsiveness.
trigger_condition: Is an element entering or expanding?

recipe: Do not reach for bounce or elastic easing by reflex. It is the loudest default-AI motion tell and it makes serious interfaces feel like toys.
trigger_condition: Did the brief ask for playful or toy-like character?

recipe: Never animate width, height, top, left, or margins. They drive layout, so every frame costs a reflow and the motion stutters under any load.

Transform and opacity are the floor, not the ceiling: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask and shadow are fair game when they stay smooth. They repaint each frame, so keep them on small, isolated elements.
trigger_condition: Is the motion a plain fade-and-slide?
_original_recipe: Transform and opacity are the floor, not the ceiling. Blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, shadow, and gradient position are animatable and far less worn out.
_review_reason: dropped the source's 'when they stay smooth' caveat; these properties repaint every frame and conflict with :114 unqualified

recipe: One authored motion moment per page. Scattered effects and identical entrance animations on every section sum to no moment at all.
trigger_condition: Does every section animate on scroll?

recipe: Animate from an already-visible default. An element hidden until its animation fires reads as missing content whenever the animation is skipped, delayed, or fails.
trigger_condition: Does the element start at opacity zero?

recipe: Stagger siblings only when the group genuinely reads as a list, and cap the total delay. Treating every scrolled section as a staggered list is a tic.
trigger_condition: Is the animated group actually a list?

recipe: Under prefers-reduced-motion remove spatial travel (parallax, large slides and zoom are the vestibular triggers) but keep opacity, colour and state transitions. Reduced motion means fewer and gentler, not none.
_original_recipe: Under reduced-motion preference remove spatial travel but keep opacity, colour, and state transitions. Reduced motion means fewer and gentler, not none; action feedback must stay legible.
_review_reason: merged the vestibular-trigger detail from duplicate :151

recipe: Honour iOS Reduce Motion and Android Remove Animations: crossfade instead of parallax and large slides, or transition instantly where the system asks for it.
trigger_condition: Is this a native iOS or Android surface?

recipe: Motion must be interruptible. An animation that ignores a second click makes the interface feel like it stopped listening to the user.
trigger_condition: Can the user act again mid-animation?

recipe: Budget one frame: 16.7ms at 60Hz, 8.3ms at 120Hz. Verify on the slowest device you support; 'transform is fast' is an assumption, not a measurement.
_original_recipe: Target 16ms per frame and verify on the slowest device you support. Transform means fast is an assumption, not a measurement.
_review_reason: 16ms is only the 60Hz budget; 120Hz displays halve it

recipe: Apply will-change only during a known animation and remove it afterwards. Left on permanently it costs memory and can make the thing measurably slower.
trigger_condition: Are you setting will-change in a stylesheet?

recipe: Stop nonessential loops when offscreen or hidden. A looping animation in a background tab is battery drain nobody asked for and nobody sees.
trigger_condition: Does any animation loop indefinitely?

recipe: Bound blur, filter, shadow, and canvas work to isolated regions. A full-page backdrop-filter is a per-frame cost paid across every pixel on screen.
trigger_condition: Does an effect apply across a large area?

recipe: To calm motion, shorten travel to roughly 10-20px rather than 40px and soften the easing before deleting the animation. Distance reads as loudness.
trigger_condition: Does the motion feel too energetic?

recipe: Do not add animation in order to make polish visible. If the motion has no job, its only effect on the user is delay.
On native follow system transitions: push slides, sheets rise, dismissal reverses the entrance. On Android use container transform, shared-axis, and fade-through.
trigger_condition: Is this a native screen or sheet transition?

recipe: Match the response to the effort and consequence. Major milestones can expand; a routine save should simply feel certain. Do not manufacture celebration for an ordinary click.
trigger_condition: Are you adding a celebratory or reward animation?

recipe: Delight must never delay or obscure the primary task, override platform conventions or accessibility, play sound without consent, or become unskippable and exhausting on repeat.
trigger_condition: Are you adding a micro-interaction or easter egg?

recipe: A depth shadow has offset plus soft blur. A zero-offset coloured halo is decoration. Do not use a halo where depth is meant, or an offset shadow as glow.
trigger_condition: Are you adding a box-shadow?

recipe: Theme the surfaces nobody remembers: text selection, caret colour, scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset, tabular numerals. Browser defaults are exactly what unfinished looks like.
Inspect computed spacing rather than trusting the source. Collapsed margins and inherited gaps mean the rendered rhythm is frequently not the rhythm you authored.
Write in the product native language and voice. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery. Do not vary wording for literary effect.
Every brief requirement must be present and discoverable within seconds. A requirement that shipped but cannot be found did not ship.
_note: generic process filler, nothing a model can act on
_review_reason: generic process filler, nothing a model can act on

recipe: Build with real content, functional controls, and responsive layout. Placeholder text hides the wrapping, truncation, and overflow problems that are the finish work.
Set explicit dimensions or aspect-ratio on every image and embed. Unreserved space is layout shift, and layout shift is the most visible craft failure there is.
Hold Cumulative Layout Shift under 0.1. Reserve space for media, ads, and embeds, and never inject content above what the user is already reading.
Do not serve a 3000px asset into a 300px slot. Use srcset with width descriptors, modern formats, and 80-85 percent quality, where the loss is imperceptible.
Lazy-load below-fold images only. Lazy-loading what is already visible trades a tiny byte saving for a visible pop-in on first paint.
trigger_condition: Is the image above the fold?

recipe: Touch only the named target. Do not restyle its neighbours or repair unrelated drift as a side effect; scope creep in styling is how design systems decay.
trigger_condition: Are you editing one component in an existing system?

recipe: When adjusting an existing surface, do not add colours, fonts, radii, shadows, or primitives it does not already own. Reach for a kit primitive before inventing a class.
trigger_condition: Are you modifying a surface inside an existing system?

recipe: Never split the difference between an old and a new aesthetic. Half-migrated design reads worse than either direction committed to fully.
trigger_condition: Is a redesign landing on top of an existing look?

recipe: The brief wins. Honour committed aesthetics, materials, and palettes even when unconventional; refinement preserves the incumbent identity, redesign replaces the whole visual world.
trigger_condition: Does a committed brief or design system already exist?

recipe: Name the surface mode before designing: persuade, operate, read, or experience. Each has a different success metric, so each justifies a different density and pace.
Finish by removing debug output, dead styles, unused imports, and the duplication the polish pass itself created. Use shared components where the system owns the pattern.
_note: generic cleanup checklist, not design-specific or actionable beyond common sense
_review_reason: generic cleanup checklist, not design-specific or actionable beyond common sense

recipe: Thick coloured card borders, hard-offset shadows, and decorative glass are period styles, not neutral defaults. Use them when the brief is neobrutalist, otherwise not.
trigger_condition: Did the brief name this visual style?

recipe: Use drawn icons from one coherent set. Emoji and Unicode glyphs as interface icons render differently on every platform and quietly break the visual system.
trigger_condition: Are you using emoji or Unicode symbols as icons?

recipe: Avoid circle and blob masks on photography as a default treatment. Cropping a photo into a shape usually destroys the composition that made it worth using.
trigger_condition: Are you masking a photograph into a geometric shape?

recipe: Choose light or dark from use context such as ambient light, session length, and content type, not from product category. Developer tool therefore dark is a reflex.
trigger_condition: Are you picking a default theme?

recipe: Clean up listeners, subscriptions, timers, and pending requests on unmount. An interface that gets slower the longer it is used is a craft failure, not a perf one.
trigger_condition: Does this component subscribe, poll, or set timers?

recipe: A delight moment must be specific enough that a neighbouring product could not use it unchanged. Generic whimsy is worse than neutral clarity.
trigger_condition: Are you adding personality to an interaction?

recipe: Verify across mobile, intermediate, and wide web layouts, or phone and tablet size classes in both orientations on native, in every content state. Screenshot, batch-fix, confirm once.
WCAG AA needs 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text; AAA asks 7:1. Placeholder text is body text for this purpose, not decoration.
WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 requires 3:1 at Level AA for UI component boundaries and states, focus indicators, and meaningful parts of graphics. Do not round 2.999 up.
WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 sets 24 by 24 CSS pixels as the Level AA pointer target minimum, with a spacing exception. SC 2.5.5 asks 44 by 44 at AAA.
Platform floors exceed WCAG AA: Apple wants 44 by 44 pt, Material wants 48 by 48 dp with at least 8 dp between targets. Design to the platform floor.
trigger_condition: Is this a native mobile or touch interface?

recipe: Keyboard focus must stay visible, themed from your palette, and clear 3:1 against its surroundings. Removing the default outline without replacing it is the commonest regression.
trigger_condition: Are you restyling or removing a focus outline?

recipe: Tab order must be logical and match visual order. Re-verify it after every responsive or CSS reorder.
_original_recipe: Tab order must be logical and match visual order, and modals must trap focus then restore it on close. Re-verify after every responsive reorder.
_review_reason: modal focus-trap clause duplicates :163

recipe: Every function reachable by pointer must be reachable by keyboard. Hover-only and drag-only interactions need a keyboard equivalent, not a note in the documentation.
trigger_condition: Is any action available only via hover or drag?

recipe: Test in forced-colors mode (Windows High Contrast): your colours are replaced wholesale, so state and meaning must survive through borders, text and icons, not background fills.
_original_recipe: Never encode meaning in colour alone, and test in Windows High Contrast mode where your colours are replaced wholesale and only structure survives.
_review_reason: colour-alone clause duplicates :10; keep the distinct forced-colors test

recipe: Honour prefers-reduced-motion by removing spatial travel while keeping opacity and state feedback. The vestibular triggers are parallax, large slides, and zoom, not fades.
_review_reason: near-duplicate of :108 (detail merged there)

recipe: Support 200 percent zoom and platform text scaling with containers that grow. Size text in sp on Android and use Dynamic Type styles on iOS, never hard-coded points.
Every input needs a programmatic label. A placeholder, an adjacent icon, and an aria-label contradicting the visible text are three distinct failures, not substitutes.
trigger_condition: Are you building a form control?

recipe: Alt text describes the function the image serves in context, not the image itself. Decorative images take empty alt so screen readers skip them entirely.
trigger_condition: Are you adding an image?

recipe: Use semantic HTML before ARIA. A div with role button needs keyboard handling, focus behaviour, and state you would get free from a real button element.
trigger_condition: Are you adding a role attribute to a generic element?

recipe: Headings must nest without skipping levels. They are the screen-reader navigation index, not a size picker, so style visual scale separately from semantic level.
trigger_condition: Are you choosing a heading tag for its size?

recipe: Inputs under 16px trigger force-zoom on focus in iOS Safari, yanking the layout sideways. Keep mobile input text at 16px or larger.
trigger_condition: Is this a text input rendered on mobile web?

recipe: On iOS use semantic system colours such as label, secondaryLabel, systemBackground and separator. They adapt to dark mode and Increase Contrast without extra work.
trigger_condition: Is this a native iOS surface?
_original_recipe: On native use semantic system colours such as label, secondaryLabel, systemBackground, and separator. They adapt to dark mode and increased-contrast settings without extra work.
_review_reason: the named colours (label, secondaryLabel, systemBackground, separator) are iOS UIKit only; trigger claimed Android too

recipe: Never disable or overlay the iOS left-edge back gesture or Android system Back. They are the platform escape hatch and users reach for them reflexively.
trigger_condition: Does this screen intercept edge gestures?

recipe: Test with an actual screen reader and keyboard-only navigation before calling anything accessible. Automated scans catch roughly the mechanical half of the failures.
Verify contrast for disabled and overlaid states and for text over images, in both themes. Disabled content is exempt from the ratio but still has to be readable.
_note: near-duplicate of :5 (verify contrast in every state, overlay, image and theme)
_review_reason: near-duplicate of :5 (verify contrast in every state, overlay, image and theme)

recipe: Accessibility markup and labelling are protected during simplification. If a decluttering pass removed labels or landmarks, it removed function rather than clutter.
trigger_condition: Are you simplifying or removing interface elements?
_note: near-duplicate of :66 (removal floor protects accessibility markup)
_review_reason: near-duplicate of :66 (removal floor protects accessibility markup)

recipe: When a dialog opens, move focus into it, keep focus inside while open, and return focus to the trigger on close. Otherwise keyboard users land nowhere.
trigger_condition: Are you building a modal, drawer, or popover?
